summary:
Elazığ province stands under the national framework of Turkey. The province's own documented signal is a state-facilitated anti-LGBT mobilisation: on 19 December 2022 an anti-LGBT hate rally was held at Elazığ's Cumhuriyet (Republic) Square under the banner "LGBT sapkınlıktır" ("LGBT is perversion"), with ruling AKP deputy mayor Nazif Bilginoğlu in attendance. The rally statement denounced consensual same-sex relationships and "homosexual marriage" as a "revolting loss of reason" attributed to Western states, used the terms "perverse" and "degenerate mentality", and tied gender and sexual themes to Turkey's denunciation of the Istanbul Convention. This is locally active hostility with official participation, and it indicates what a visibly LGBTQ traveller could face in this province.

Elazığ's provincial authorities operate within a national framework in which a leaked omnibus draft law dated 29 October 2025, the 11th Judicial Package, would amend the penal and civil codes to criminalise conduct deemed "contrary to biological sex and general morality" with up to three years' imprisonment, impose a minimum age of 25 and onerous eligibility conditions on gender-affirming healthcare, and expose both trans people and the professionals providing their care to criminal charges. The government's stated justification is protecting "the family" and "public morals"; the package also carries unrelated measures such as longer child sentences and online-content removal. Whether it has since passed is unresolved in the sources.
tangentialFactors: Elazığ's 2022 rally sits within a national pattern in which the authorities have repeatedly banned and forcibly dispersed Pride marches since 2015 using tear gas, water cannons and mass detentions. In ILGA-Europe's 2026 Rainbow Europe ranking Turkey placed 47th of 49, ahead only of Azerbaijan and Russia. In early 2026 the government was considering criminalising public advocacy of "behaviour contrary to biological sex and general morality", the same framing that underpinned the 11th Judicial Package.
localsOnly: Elazığ residents live under national law in which homosexuality has been decriminalised since 1858 and gender-reassignment surgery has been legal since 1988, and in which discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation or gender identity is prohibited in law. Same-sex relationships, marriage, civil unions and same-sex adoption receive no legal recognition, and LGBTI people are barred from serving openly in the military. Local political figures in Elazığ have publicly aligned with anti-LGBT positions, as the 19 December 2022 Cumhuriyet Square rally with the AKP deputy mayor's participation demonstrates.
outOfScopeNotes: Whether the 11th Judicial Package has been enacted since the 29 October 2025 leak is unresolved in the sources. The inventory contains no Elazığ-specific enforcement data, detention figures, or incidents of violence against trans residents or visitors in the province; the hostility signal rests on the single documented 2022 rally. No Elazığ-specific information on healthcare access, facilities, or policing practice toward trans people is sourced.
